st: Artificial intelligence between guillotines, powerlessness and perdition

sec.t: ff.55.1 How does it feel, inside a revolution?
sec.p: Before any other reflection, I recommend Lex Fridman's ever-timely podcast with the founder of OpenAI.

sec.t: ff.55.2 Fields to plough (and data to reclaim)
sec.p: Sam Korus of Ark Invest points out how every revolution gives value to new raw materials and generates new outputs, citing Carlota Perez's book Technological Revolutions and Financial Capital.

sec.t: ff.55.3 Forget Julius Caesar: the new emperors
sec.p: In 🎼 ff.52 Founding a Nation in your garage we talked about the growing centralisation of some services (and the problems that come with it). What struck me was the collapse in the number of employees needed to reach 1M in revenue at S&P 500 companies.

sec.t: ff.55.4 A few nice things since the last update
sec.p: Recently stable diffusion has outclassed GANs, Generative Adversarial Networks. And yet, if we want to move from one text-prompted image to another, GANs guarantee more consistent video transitions.
